PORT ANGELES, Wash. (Gray News) - Human remains that were found in a Washington park in 2000 were identified through advanced genetic testing.

A researcher found skeletal remains inside of a sleeping bag in a tent along the Sol Duc River drainage area in Olympic National Park in 2000.

Those remains were sent to the county medical examiner’s office. There, a pathologist determined the remains were those of a man between 30 and 50 years old who had died anywhere from six months to four years prior.

Twenty-four years later, the medical examiner’s office sent a DNA sample to the Othram laboratory. Using newer technology, the lab identified the man’s possible family connections.

After more than 20 years, he was identified as Joseph Louis Serrao Jr.

Family members said he was from Hawaii and had been in Washington before he was reported missing. Their last contact with him was in 1998.
